answer: Here is one mechanism that works: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because tundra only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, prism is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any summit approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
